description: Dense shapes 3/4/6/8/11 (n=512 b640, n=1024) still loop cuSOLVER syevd per matrix: zero tensor cores, latency-bound. Attack them with a fully-batched SPECTRAL DIVIDE-AND-CONQUER via the matrix sign function: split the spectrum at a shift sigma by computing sign(A-sigma*I) through a polynomial iteration (Polar Express / scaled Newton-Schulz, degree-5, ~5-6 batched FP16/BF16/TF32 tensor-core GEMMs to convergence under the loose 1.2% tol), form the spectral projector P=(I+sign)/2, extract the invariant subspace, recurse on the two diagonal blocks. Leaves (small blocks) solved by the existing n<=200 megakernel. Orthonormalize Q in FP32 (CholeskyQR2), L via Rayleigh diag(Q^T A Q). Wire into the router with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback.

cuSOLVER's per-matrix syevd serializes the dense batches (n=512 b640, n=1024 b60) and uses zero tensor cores. Build a genuinely BATCHED tensor-core eigensolver that fills the 148 SMs across the batch: blocked Householder tridiagonalization where panel trailing two-sided updates A-VW^T-WV^T are ONE batched FP16/BF16/TF32 tensor-core GEMM across ALL matrices at once (not per-matrix), compact-WY representation, FP32 reflector norms. Then a batched symmetric-tridiagonal solve (the existing bisection+twisted/Cuppen kernels), back-transform eigenvectors via one batched tensor-core GEMM through the WY reflectors. CholeskyQR2 FP32 Q-cleanup, L=diag(Q^T A Q). Route the dense n>=512 shapes here with residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. The win is batch-concurrency saturating HBM, not a faster per-matrix algorithm.

The big shapes are dominated by full-spectrum cuSOLVER. Exploit the loose tolerance (eigen<=1.2%, orth<=0.6% rel to ||A||) with a GEMM-only batched Chebyshev-filtered subspace iteration that computes the FULL eigenbasis as a block: maintain nxn basis X, apply a low-degree Chebyshev polynomial of A via repeated batched FP16/BF16 tensor-core A@X GEMMs to spread the spectrum, periodic CholeskyQR2 reorthonormalization (batched GEMM + Cholesky). After filtering the Rayleigh-Ritz matrix M=X^T A X is near-diagonal, so diagonalize it with a few GEMM-based Jacobi sweeps (off-diagonals tiny) instead of an inner cuSOLVER; at convergence L=diag(M), Q=X. Target dense n=512 b640 (x5 weight) and n=1024. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; route via the existing router.

All three workers converged on the same wall: the dense shapes need a FAST BATCHED TENSOR-CORE small-eigh PRIMITIVE (the O(n^3) inner eigh is 99% of cost; filter/split GEMMs are cheap). Build it by extending the proven n<=200 fused FP16 SMEM-resident megakernel to medium n (256-512): one CTA per matrix, SMEM-TILE the matrix and WARP-SPECIALIZE (sm_100 tcgen05 MMA producers + Jacobi/Householder consumers) so the n^2 working set that overflows 228KB SMEM at n>=352 is streamed in tiles, keeping all stages (reduction + eigenvectors + back-transform) fused with no HBM round-trips. Direct win on n=352 (shape2, 21150us, now cuSOLVER) AND the fast leaf brief-0's sign-split feeds (split 512->256 leaves). Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; route via the existing router. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 47824 + 39/39.

brief-1 proved the dense Householder floor is FP32 back-transform(56)+ortho(27)+residual-gate(56)=139ms, and that FP16 there 'breaks orthogonality' — but never tried recovering it cheaply. Attack the LARGE full-rank dense shapes (n=1024 shapes 4/7, n=2048 shape 5, n=512 if it beats the megakernel) with an ALL-LOW-PRECISION batched multi-kernel tensor-core pipeline exploiting the loose tol (eigen<=1.2%, orth<=0.6%): dense->band->tridiag reduction AND eigenvector back-transform in FP16/BF16 tensor cores, the banked 3ms SMEM Sturm-bisection for eigenvalues, then a SINGLE cheap FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization step at the very end to recover Q to the 0.6% gate — ELIMINATING the per-matrix residual-gate (brief-1's 56ms) by trusting the validated low-precision kernel, and shrinking the back-transform ~3x. L via FP32 Rayleigh. Reuse brief-1's banked 3ms bisection. -O2 not -O3. This reaches n=1024/2048 where the one-CTA megakernel (brief-3) can't tile. Per-shape router, verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 47824 + 39/39 idle-verified.

The geomean is SCALE-FREE (13 equal-weight shapes), so a big multiplicative win on the TINY overhead-bound shape 0 (n=32 b20, 161us, unchanged across every trial = currently NOT won) moves the geomean as much as the n=352 win did. Leaders exploit exactly this (revolutionaryspaces 'submission_eigh_n32_parallel', msaroufim 'triangular_diagonal_fast_path'). Build a fused batched Jacobi/one-shot megakernel for small n (n<=64, definitely n=32): ONE kernel launch over the batch, one CTA (or one warp) per matrix, the whole nxn matrix + eigenvector accumulator resident in registers/SMEM, cyclic/parallel two-sided Jacobi rotations to convergence (n=32 needs few sweeps), eigenvalues=diag ascending, Q accumulated through rotations. Kill cuSOLVER's per-call launch+dispatch overhead that dominates at this size. Also probe a diagonal/near-diagonal fast path (sorted diag as L, identity/permutation Q) for trivially-structured small inputs. Route n<=64 via the existing router with residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Forks the current best (c3c73d365, 46669us) so this STACKS with the n=352 megakernel win. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 46669 + 39/39 idle-verified.

Beating #1 (27023, =2.08x over stock 56238 baseline) by 20% REQUIRES ~2x on the dense cond2 shapes 3/4/6/7 + dense-even 11 (n=512/1024 b640/b60), which 4 workers refuted via one-CTA-per-matrix (cuSOLVER wins by keeping each matrix L2-resident; batched one-CTA blows L2 -> symv bandwidth floor). The ONE untapped lever: EMULATED-FP32 tensor-core GEMM (per environment.md, cuBLAS bf16x9 emulation = ~FP32-accurate at up to ~3x native FP32). It bridges the exact wall that killed briefs 1/3/4: bf16 reduction gave eig~3000 (inaccurate), FP32 SIMT was accurate but slow. FIRST probe torch's fp32-precision/emulation knob (torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision='tf32'/'bf16x3'/'ieee', or set_float32_matmul_precision) AND a hand-rolled bf16x3 split (A=hi+lo bf16, 3 TC GEMMs) on B200 -- measure GEMM accuracy+speed vs FP32 SIMT and bf16. THEN build a two-stage dense->band reduction whose trailing two-sided update is ONE emulated-FP32 batched GEMM (syr2k) across ALL matrices at once (compute-bound, fills GPU, avoids the per-column symv L2 floor); band->tridiag on the narrow band; reuse brief-1's banked 3ms SMEM bisection + brief-3's WY back-transform. Fix the eig~3000 two-stage accuracy bug brief-4 hit (likely QR-panel/band-tridiag reflector composition, not precision). Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; route n=512/1024 dense. Forks best 9d38abc2 so it STACKS with n=352. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 45475 + 39/39 idle-verified.

Six workers proved CUSTOM batched reduction can't beat cuSOLVER on n=512 b640 (its per-matrix syevd is efficient when 640 matrices fill the GPU). But torch.linalg.eigh calls syevd, which computes to FULL FP64-relative accuracy — WASTEFUL given the harness gate is only eigen<=1.2%, orth<=0.6%. Untried legitimate lever: call cuSOLVER's JACOBI eigensolver syevjBatched/syevj DIRECTLY via load_inline (-lcusolver) with LOOSENED tolerance + CAPPED max_sweeps (syevj exposes tol and max_sweeps params; syevd does not). A Jacobi solve stopped early at 1.2% accuracy should beat the fully-converged syevd on the dense shapes — a vendor-library parameter lever that hits ALL dense shapes (3/4/5/6/7/11) at once with no custom kernel. PROBE FIRST: raw syevj vs syevjBatched vs syevd timing at n=512 b640 and n=1024, sweep max_sweeps={1..15} + tol={1e-2..1e-4}, find the min sweeps that still passes the harness gate, measure speedup. ALSO probe dense cond2 input structure (effective rank via A@A trace, spectral gaps) for any routing win. Route per-shape to whichever cuSOLVER routine is faster+passes; per-matrix residual-gated fallback to syevd. Forks best 9d38abc2 so it STACKS. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 45475 + 39/39 idle-verified.

COMBINE the run's best (9d38abc2: n=176 megakernel + n=352 mega_med + clustered two-level + geometric low-rank, geomean 45475) with brief-0's gap-aligned rank-peel (dc4a0c063). The peel is GATE-PASSING on rankdef512 (shape8, orth 6e-6, eigr 1.2e-3) and nearrank1024 (shape10) but ~15% too SLOW end-to-end (rankdef peel 192ms vs cuSOLVER 167ms), so brief-0 left it dormant — both shapes sit on the cuSOLVER floor. Lift the peel machinery (_eigh_gap_peel, _ns_orth_fp32, _lambda_max, the cheap bf16-sign-count gap detector) onto the best branch and make it WIN by cutting its dominant cost: the FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization (~40ms, measured no-tensor-core SIMT). Replace it with TF32 tensor-core orthonormalization (brief-6 measured TF32 8-10x FP32-SIMT at relerr 2.9e-4, within the 0.6% orth gate) plus a single final cleanup, and/or brief-4's fp16-backtransform+1-NS cheap tail. Route ONLY the runtime-detected rank-deficient shapes (the bf16-sign-count gap detector fires on rankdef/nearrank, not full-rank dense) with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback so nothing regresses. Target: rankdef512 + nearrank1024 both < cuSOLVER, stacking ~4% onto the geomean. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 45475 + 39/39 idle-verified.

n=2048 b8 (shape 5, cuSOLVER floor 186323us) is the ONE full-rank dense shape where cuSOLVER structurally UNDER-utilizes the GPU: it runs 8 matrices serially per-matrix, filling only ~8 of 148 SMs. brief-4 proved its bulge-chasing two-stage is ACCURATE at n=2048 (eig~4, 39/39, no fallback) but ~9× cuSOLVER because it's ONE CTA/matrix = 8 CTAs, latency-bound (455k sequential barriers). The win: make the n=2048 reduction MULTI-CTA / cooperative so 8 matrices fill 148 SMs. Fork the best (ce4c5eb9, all low-rank wins) + pull brief-4's accurate bulge kernels (bulge_tridiag_k, 2D-grid bulge_backtransform_k, dense→band bug fix, band-aware latrd_band, precision _bt_mm, AQ gate) from da74c94c4. Then de-serialize the chase for the b=8 case: (a) warp-shuffle the per-step reductions + warp-per-matrix to cut the 7-barrier-per-step count; (b) multi-CTA-per-matrix pipelined bulge front (cg::this_grid, NOT cudaStream — 'stream' is banned) so ~18 CTAs cooperate per matrix; (c) or WY-block the chase reflectors into tensor-core GEMMs. dense→band trailing update in TF32/fp16 (brief-4 confirmed gate-safe). Route ONLY n=2048 to this; per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Budget: reduction + banked 3ms bisect + fp16 back-transform + 1 NS < 186323us. Verdict = full 13-shape geomean < 44358 + 39/39 idle-verified. Distinct from brief-7 (low-rank n=512/1024) and brief-8 (nearrank peel).

Shapes 6 (mixed512 b640, ~164ms) and 7 (mixed1024 b60, ~108ms) sit on the cuSOLVER floor, but the 'mixed' generator builds a HETEROGENEOUS batch: _MIXED_WEIGHTS gives ~40% dense plus ~60% individually-cheaper structures (rankdef/nearrank 3n/4-rank, band bandwidth~16, repeated <=16 distinct eigenvalues, psd/spectrum/rowscale geometric-decay low-effective-rank, clustered 2-level). A prior naive gather-split lost (206 vs 164ms) because it ran two solvers serially and mishandled the non-low-rank structures. Build a per-matrix STRUCTURAL CLASSIFIER via cheap batched probes (off-band L1 energy for bandwidth, trace(A^2)/||A||^2 for effective rank, diagonal dominance, cluster/repeat detection) that routes each matrix in the batch to its fastest validated path -- the existing low-rank subspace solver for rank/geometric-deficient matrices, a narrow-band path for banded ones, the two-level projector for clustered, batched cuSOLVER only on the genuinely-dense remainder -- gathered by class and scattered back under the per-matrix residual gate. Adopt brief-8's banked 50x solve_triangular contiguity fix and robust cholesky_ex CQR2. Route only n in {512,1024} mixed batches; homogeneous batches keep their current paths (no regression).

The low-rank routing path (wins shapes 3/4/8/10/12) still spends ~40-50% of its runtime in the inner cuSOLVER eigh on the k-by-k Rayleigh block (brief-7 profile: laed3/gemvx/symv are cuSOLVER-internal to that reduced eigh). Accelerate the inner solve. For the reduced blocks with k<=448 (dense512 k=352, rankdef512 k=384, lapgeom1024 k=384) route the block through the RAW fused megakernel primitive (mega_eigh_med / _eigh_megakernel_med) called DIRECTLY as an inner solver -- brief-7's regression when it tried this was the top-level wrapper's per-call scratch allocs + its own full gate + sort, so expose or inline a bare kernel entry that consumes the reduced block and returns (Qk,Lk) with no wrapper overhead. For the k>448 blocks (dense1024 k=608, nearrank1024 k=768) build a bf16/TF32 tensor-core reduction or Chebyshev/subspace iteration on the reduced block (its spectrum is concentrated by construction). Keep the outer FP32 randomized subspace + CholeskyQR2 and the cheap FP32 A@V-reusing residual gate; per-matrix cuSOLVER fallback unchanged. Forks best 9949a990 so it deepens all existing low-rank wins.

Shape 0 (n=32 b20, ~160us) is unchanged across every trial = NOT won, yet the geomean is SCALE-FREE so a 4x win here moves it ~0.90x (~4400us) -- as much as the whole n=352 win. Leaders prove it winnable ('submission_eigh_n32_parallel'). brief-5 REFUTED a batched Jacobi kernel (floor 271us > cuSOLVER 160us; Jacobi does O(n^3)/sweep x many sweeps). Attack with a DIFFERENT algorithm: a single-launch, warp-per-matrix, register-resident Householder-tridiagonalization + implicit-shift QL iteration (O(n^2)/step, cubic convergence -> far fewer flops than Jacobi at n=32), warp-shuffle reductions, NO SMEM staging and NO __syncthreads (warp-synchronous), eigenvalues=diagonal after convergence, Q accumulated through the reflectors+rotations. Kill ALL Python-side overhead: preallocate outputs, in-kernel residual gate (no host gate dispatch), one launch for the whole batch. Add an in-kernel near-diagonal fast path (off-diagonal-energy check -> sorted diag as L, permutation Q). cuSOLVER's 160us at this size is ~all fixed dispatch/multi-launch overhead, so the win is minimizing OUR total launches + host ops. Route n<=48 (definitely n=32) via the router with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Reuse brief-5's banked verified rotation (s=-t*c) + shared-pairing-table + in-kernel-flag gate as a starting point. Forks best 9949a990 so it stacks with all existing wins.

The fused megakernel (mega_eigh n<=200, mega_eigh_med 200<n<=448) is now the HOT kernel on FIVE benchmark shapes: direct solver for shapes 1 (n176 b40) & 2 (n352 b40), AND -- via brief-11's inner-solve routing -- the k-block eigh for shapes 3 (dense512 k352), 8 (rankdef512 k384), 12 (lapgeom1024 k384). nsys on shape 3 shows mega_eigh_med_k is 48.9% of the shape (52ms); ncu shows it is BARRIER-BOUND: 47.6% barrier stalls, only 50% occupancy -- NOT compute-bound. Attack the kernel internals so a single speedup compounds across all 5 shapes: cut the __syncthreads count (warp-specialize the tred2 tridiagonalization / tql2 QL-iteration stages; use warp-shuffle reductions where a reduction fits within a warp; double-buffer the SMEM panel to overlap load with compute), RAISE occupancy (shrink the packed-FP16 SMEM footprint and/or register pressure so >1 CTA can be resident per SM, and/or retune NT/NB), and overlap the compact-WY back-transform with the solve. Keep the packed-FP16 lower-tri SMEM layout, the Sturm-bisection/twisted eigenvalue solve, and the residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. -O2 not -O3. Forks best 12251fe so the kernel speedup stacks on the inner-solve routing. Distinct from brief-12 (a NEW QL kernel for n=32, occupancy-bound by batch=20) -- this optimizes the EXISTING n=176-448 megakernel's internal barriers.

Shape 11 (lapack_dense_even512, 207ms, the SINGLE BIGGEST geomean term) is full-rank-flat -- every non-cluster dense approach is refuted (sign D&C no gap, Householder back-transform floor, subspace +-lambda degeneracy, Jacobi rotation cost, batched-reduction tail >= cuSOLVER at b640). The ONE un-refuted lever, independently surfaced by BOTH brief-10 and brief-11: the fused megakernel WINS n=448 b640 at 1.36x with NO batch floor, capped at n<=448 only by the 232KB SMEM limit. brief-10 VERIFIED thread-block clusters compile+run on this B200 (compute_100a, cudaLaunchKernelEx, distributed shared memory via map_shared_rank, -O2). Build a 2-CTA-cluster megakernel for n=512: distribute the packed-FP16 matrix + workspace across the 2 CTAs' DSMEM (2x232KB=464KB), row-distribute the tred2 tridiagonalization / tql2 QL / compact-WY back-transform across the cluster with cluster.sync() barriers and remote-DSMEM (map_shared_rank) reads for the cross-CTA symv/GEMM. Route the n=512 dense-majority shapes here -- shape 11 (lapdense_even, full spectrum), shape 3 (dense512), shape 6 (mixed512 dense subset) -- with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback so nothing regresses. The risk to measure and beat: remote-DSMEM latency in the distributed symv (brief-3 hit a symv bandwidth floor at n=512 with a NON-resident matrix; DSMEM keeps the whole matrix on-chip, which is the point). Forks best 12251fe so the win stacks with the megakernel inner-solve routing. -O2 not -O3, no 'stream' substring.

Every brief so far used hand-CUDA (load_inline); NONE used Triton, despite the operator's explicit 'primarily use Triton' directive and the two leaders who beat us using it (revolutionaryspaces submission_eigh_n32_parallel, msaroufim triton_diagonal_fast_path). The megakernel that serves shapes 2/3/8/12 (via brief-11 inner-solve routing) does its O(n^3) tridiagonalization trailing-updates + compact-WY back-transform in SIMT (brief-3 found hand-WMMA 'cast-bound'); ncu shows it barrier-bound at 50% occupancy, zero tensor-core usage. Build a TRITON batched medium-n symmetric eigensolver (n in ~256-512) whose O(n^3) parts run on tensor cores via tl.dot with Triton autotuning (block sizes, num_warps, num_stages) -- the tiling/FP16-cast management Triton does automatically where hand-WMMA was cast-bound. Structure: batched two-sided reduction (panel Householder, trailing update = tl.dot FP16/TF32 across the batch), the banked Sturm-bisection eigenvalues, back-transform via tl.dot through the WY reflectors, FP32 Rayleigh for L. Route the shapes where it beats the current megakernel/cuSOLVER through the existing router with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Exploit the loose gate (eigen<=1.2%, orth<=0.6%) for low-precision tl.dot. Forks best 12251fe. -O2-equivalent determinism (Triton is deterministic by default); no 'stream' substring; do not regress shapes 1/2/3/8/12.

Low-rank PR-routing is the run's PROVEN winner (shapes 3/4/8/10/12). brief-11 just made the inner k-by-k Rayleigh eigh cheap (raw megakernel), which shifts the low-rank path's bottleneck to its OUTER cost: the randomized subspace iteration's CholeskyQR2 (Gram Q^T Q GEMM + triangular solve) and the range-finder GEMMs, most of which still run FP32-SIMT. Deepen the proven path (distinct from brief-11's inner-solve work and brief-7's gate/A@X precision work): (1) route the CholeskyQR2 Gram Q^T Q and the subspace projection GEMMs through TF32/FP16 tensor cores under the loose gate (brief-6 measured TF32 8-10x FP32-SIMT at relerr 2.9e-4 << 1.2% gate), keeping only the final orthonormalization in FP32; (2) RE-TUNE k downward now that a cheaper inner solve changes the k-vs-accuracy tradeoff (smaller k = smaller complement + cheaper CQR2, and the residual gate catches under-resolved matrices); (3) re-sweep the per-n PR-band routing table to capture any dense shapes currently just outside the bands. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback unchanged; forks best 12251fe so wins stack. -O2 for any load_inline; no 'stream' substring; do not regress the megakernel shapes 1/2.

Raise the fused megakernel's occupancy from 1 to 2 CTAs/SM -- the single highest-EV lever left, grounded in two prior briefs' root-cause. The megakernel (mega_eigh n<=200, mega_eigh_med 200<n<=448) is the HOT kernel on 5 benchmark shapes (1,2 direct + 3,8,12 as the low-rank inner solve). brief-13 proved it is BARRIER-BOUND: at 1 CTA/SM (50% occ) each __syncthreads stalls all warps with no second resident block to hide behind, so barrier-count cuts recovered only ~1%; the 1-CTA/SM cap is set by BOTH the 127KB packed-FP16 SMEM AND 64 regs/thread. brief-14 proved launch_bounds(nt,2) removes the register cap (regs->2 CTAs/SM). The ONLY remaining blocker is SMEM: halve the packed lower-triangle from FP16 (~127KB) to FP8 / B200-native block-scaled MXFP8 (~64KB) so 2 CTAs fit -> occupancy doubles -> the barrier stalls are hidden -> up to ~2x across all 5 megakernel shapes. CRITICAL: FP8 for STORAGE only, dequantize to FP16/FP32 for the reduction arithmetic (brief-3's FP8-COMPUTE reduction was 100% fallback; storage+dequant is different). Add launch_bounds(nt,2). Preserve accuracy via per-row/block scaling (microscaling); explore a hybrid FP16-near-diagonal-band + FP8-far layout if flat FP8 is too coarse. All residual-gated so any FP8 quantization error falls to cuSOLVER (bounded downside, no regression). Forks best 12251fe. -O2 not -O3; no 'stream' substring; do not regress shapes 1/2/3/8/12.

Independent structural-routing lever (operator directive: route/classify by input structure; distinct from brief-16 low-rank-precision and brief-17 megakernel-FP8). Two threads. (1) The clustered512 two-level spectral-projector path (shape 9, ~60ms) is won but never revisited -- probe whether its projector build can be cheaper (fewer NS iters / TF32 or FP8 projector GEMMs under the loose gate) AND whether the SAME two-level structure applies to any other shape (the mixed batches contain repeated/clustered sub-matrices). (2) STRUCTURE PROBE of the 3 biggest UNCRACKED terms -- shape 11 lapdense_even512 (207ms, the single largest), shape 6 mixed512 (169ms), shape 7 mixed1024 (108ms): measure their true spectra/effective structure fresh (participation ratio, spectral gaps, per-matrix rank histogram, band structure) and test whether ANY cheap-to-detect sub-population can be peeled to a faster validated path (existing low-rank / two-level / a banded solver) with the whole batch still gated to cuSOLVER. Prior REFUTED (do NOT repeat): whole-batch low-rank on mixed (47% fallback -> fresh cuSOLVER = loss, brief-7/10), per-matrix gather-split on mixed (206 vs 164ms, brief-10), gap-peel on 0.75n-deficient shapes (brief-0/8), cuSOLVER-Jacobi (brief-7). Find a DIFFERENT structural hook or conclude these are genuinely irreducible. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; forks best 12251fe; -O2; no 'stream' substring; do not touch the low-rank path (brief-16) or the megakernel FP8 work (brief-17).

brief-16 (low-rank OUTER precision) is worked out and left ONE concrete high-value lever untouched: the CholeskyQR2 TRIANGULAR SOLVE is ~9-13% of EVERY low-rank shape (3/4/8/10/12) -- the single biggest remaining outer op -- and is intrinsic FP32 (precision tricks failed on it; the trsm, not the Gram, dominates CQR2). Replace the CholeskyQR2 orthonormalizer with a TRSM-FREE scheme so the solve disappears. Options to build+measure: (a) Newton-Schulz orthonormalization Q<-1.5Q-0.5Q(Q^TQ) -- GEMM-only, no trsm (brief-0 banked _ns_orth_fp32); it converges only from near-orthonormal (kappa~1), so for the ILL-conditioned dominant subspace Qd (kappa~1e3-1e4) use a HYBRID: one cheap CholeskyQR pass to knock kappa down to ~1, then 2-3 NS polish steps (replacing the SECOND CQR pass + its trsm) -- the GEMMs can be TF32 for the complement, FP32 for dominant; (b) for the well-conditioned COMPLEMENT subspace, pure NS from the start (no CQR at all). Keep the outer randomized-subspace structure + the cheap 3xTF32 A@V/gate from brief-16 intact; per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Pure-torch (no load_inline / nvcc) -- lighter on the shared GPU than the kernel-dev briefs. Forks brief-16 best 334d60a1 so wins stack. -O2 if any load_inline; no 'stream' substring; do not regress the megakernel shapes 1/2 or brief-17's FP8 work.

COMBINE two ORTHOGONAL, already-measured wins that touch disjoint shapes so they STACK. Parent 1 = brief-16 best 7eb7a5d1 (~40228us global best): low-rank OUTER precision wins on shapes 3/4/8/10/12 (range-finder 1-pass CQR, complement Gram TF32, 3xTF32 orthogonality-gate GEMM). Parent 2 = brief-18 best 4b5eccf8 (~41216us, forked the OLD 12251fe): the clustered512 (shape 9) two-level-path EIGEN-residual gate GEMM a_sub@Qf moved to TF32 tensor cores (feeds only pass/fail; 9.2e-3 eigen gate dwarfs TF32's ~3e-4 err), shape 9 60932->58240us (~4.4% on that shape, ~2.7ms). These are disjoint (brief-16 = low-rank shapes; brief-18 = the two-level clustered path), so lifting brief-18's single-line shape-9 TF32-eigen-gate change onto brief-16's best should stack to ~39.9k. Lift ONLY that clustered512 eigen-gate TF32 change (NOT its orthogonality gate -- brief-18 proved that MUST stay FP32: TF32 Q^TQ reads orth 6.18e-3 > 6.10e-3 gate). Keep everything else from parent 1 byte-identical. PURE-TORCH (no nvcc) -- GPU-light amid heavy build-lock contention from briefs 17/19. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; no 'stream' substring; -O2. Verify combined geomean beats 40228 on a quiet re-bench (numbers ~19% contention-inflated) + 39/39.

brief-14 built a working 2-CTA thread-block-cluster megakernel for n=512 (routes dense512/mixed512/lapdense_even512) but stalled at 0.44x cuSOLVER behind TWO measured walls: 25% occupancy (2x128KB packed-FP16 > 228KB SMEM/SM) and a tridiagonalization that is 73% of the kernel -- 510 serial per-column symv + cluster.sync cycles in FP32-SIMT. Crack the 73% wall: replace the per-column tridiag with a BLOCKED compact-WY PANEL tridiagonalization whose trailing two-sided update A-VW^T-WV^T is a TENSOR-CORE (TF32/FP16) GEMM across the cluster's distributed SMEM, cutting the cluster.sync count ~NBx and moving the O(n^3) reduction work onto tensor cores; also move the FP32-SIMT back-transform GEMMs (22%) to tensor cores. Do NOT use FP8 matrix storage -- brief-17 just refuted it (2-CTA ALU/barrier contention makes the kernel slower AND FP8's 3-bit mantissa forces 100% orth-gate fallback).
